history: initial implementation used cuVS CAGRA for anomaly-distance ANN search, tuned for million-point indexes; on a 300-point calibration window this gave tick-by-tick mean latency of 3.59ms, SLOWER than CPU baseline (2.26ms)
per-stage profiling isolated the cost: umap_transform ~48%, cagra_search_evaluate ~41%, hdbscan_predict ~11%
hypothesis: CAGRA's graph-based index construction is overkill at this data scale; tested cuVS brute_force as a direct alternative
measured result: brute_force search is 11.24x faster than CAGRA at 300-point scale (0.11ms vs 1.24ms mean per single-vector query)
after switching AnomalyDetectorGPU to brute_force, tick-by-tick mean latency dropped to 2.38ms, matching CPU baseline
remaining bottleneck after the fix is umap_transform alone at ~73% of total latency; this has no drop-in faster alternative within cuML for this use case
known_limitations: the brute_force vs CAGRA finding is specific to this calibration window size (300 points); CAGRA is expected to outperform brute_force as the historical attractor map grows to thousands or millions of points via Section 4.4 refits, and this tradeoff should be re-evaluated at production scale, not assumed fixed

this uses Python cuML/cuVS wrappers, not the C++/CUDA execution plane specified in the architecture; the spec explicitly requires no Python/interpreter in the hot path for production tick-to-trade latency, which this reference implementation does not provide

the <1us tick-to-trade target from the specification requires a native C++/CUDA execution plane and DPU-level batching/pipelining not implemented here; even the improved 2.38ms figure is roughly 2400x above that target

GPU tick-by-tick and CPU tick-by-tick are now within noise of each other at this data scale; the earlier apparent GPU advantage only appears in batched processing (~28x faster), not single-tick latency
